snippets.snippet_text: "Even at my highest point — 17 patrons — and later when I closed it with four remaining, I realized something important: the people who stayed were there for me, not just the content. That meant a lot. But it also revealed something deeper. The model itself wasn't aligned with how I create. I don't create best from obligation. I create best from clarity and energetic overflow. Over time, Patreon began to feel more like maintenance than expansion."

"I also started observing specific patterns. I saw creators with YouTube channels exceeding 100,000 subscribers bring in only a small fraction of that audience to Patreon. In some cases, thousands of viewers would watch their videos consistently, yet only a handful converted into paying members."
